speaker: Wave

voice.name: Andrew
voice.note: Pre-recorded, en-US-AndrewNeural, one clip per step.

how_to_use: Each flow is a list of steps. Show a step as an assistant message (typed ~45 chars/s, instant with reduced motion) and play its audio. 'advance_on' lists the events (separated by |) that move to the next step; 'auto' means show the next step right after this one finishes; 'next' means the Next button; 'end' is the last step. Events: file_or_link_sent, project_created, card_opened, card_created, mint_done, user_message, quickstart_saved, mint_tab_opened, source_picked, file_or_paste_sent, migration_created, cards_ready.

notes.m2: Show the existing per-source how-to (uploadHint) as the text, with this line spoken. The per-source text is not voiced.
notes.tip: Show once per project, after p4.

steps.text: Let's make a project. A project turns a document or a web page into cards you can mint to Theta.
Upload a PDF with the plus button, or paste a web address and send it.
Reading it now. I'm splitting it into suggested cards and a manifest.
Your project is open on the left. Check the Manifest tab first, then the Cards tab.
Want something from our chat on a card? Highlight it, save it as a Clip, then use To project.
Click a card to review it. It also fills in the Mint tab on the right.
Mint the manifest first, then your cards. Every mint shows the TFUEL price before you approve in your wallet.
Minted! Your cards are in Mint history, and they open read-only. To change one later, you mint a new card that replaces it.
Let's mint one card. Tell me what it's about, or paste the text you want on it.
I'll shape it into a good card: a clear title, a line saying what it's for, short facts, and under 2,500 bytes.
Your card is open in the Open card tab and ready in the Mint tab. Change anything by asking me, or edit it there.
Public or private? Anyone can read a public card. A private card is encrypted in Wave Wallet Mint before it goes on chain, so only you can read it.
Check the price, then click Mint and approve in your wallet.
Minted! It's in Mint history. Click it any time to review it.
Let's build a Wave Site. It's stored on Theta as cards, and a .theta name can point people to it.
You get up to 20 pages, 50 cards and 200 kilobytes, with sections, colors, a nav and a footer. No scripts, and links stay inside your site.
Start with Quick start on the left: a name, your .theta name, and a tip wallet if you want one.
Now tell me about your site: who it's for, the pages you want, and the look.
Here's your site in Preview. Ask me for changes, or fine-tune it in the Project, Design and Advanced tabs on the right.
When it looks right, open Mint. The plan lists every card and the TFUEL total before you approve.
It's live on Theta. Last step: point your .theta name at your Home card so people can visit it.
Let's move your data to Wave. Where is it coming from? Pick a source below, or type it.
Here's how to get your data out. Follow the steps, then come back.
In the Manifest tab, give your migration a title and choose whether to track its source.
Upload your file with the plus button, up to 50 megabytes, or paste the text and send it.
Got it. I'm splitting it into one-idea cards.
Review your cards in the Open migration tab, then scan and freeze them in the editor. Remove anything you don't want on chain.
Then mint them. Choose private or public first. Big migrations mint in batches, and you see the TFUEL total before you approve.
Done! Your cards are on Theta, and they belong to you.
